issues.description: Unreachable `break` after `raise PerformanceWarning(msg)` proves the failure path was never executed.
issues.detail: The `break` immediately following `raise` is dead code — control never reaches it. That this slipped through means the failing branch was never run end-to-end. Delete the break and fix the surrounding semantics; coverage on the failure path should have caught this.

issues.description: Raising `PerformanceWarning` as an exception conflates warn-and-proceed with hard refusal.
issues.detail: `PerformanceWarning` is a Warning subclass but is used with `raise`, turning a perf advisory into a write-killing exception. The PR description itself flags this as an open design question. Decide one contract: `warnings.warn(msg, PerformanceWarning)` and proceed, or `raise ValueError`/rename the class. Don't ship both shapes at once.

issues.description: `safe_chunk_size` byte computation is wrong-shape and yields a misleading user-facing recommendation.
issues.detail: `np.prod(zarr_write_chunks) * max(1, z.dtype.itemsize)` multiplies all shard dimensions together while the divisibility failure is per-axis, and the structure of `zarr_write_chunks` may not even be a plain shape tuple. The recommended `array.chunk-size` value in the error message is therefore unreliable. State the invariant, compute bytes from a verified shape, and test the round-trip.

issues.description: Divisibility check inspects only `dw[0]` and never states its loop invariant.
issues.detail: `normalize_chunks` can return heterogeneous tuples where the last chunk is a remainder. Checking only `dw[0]` silently accepts ragged interior chunks and conflates the legitimate tail remainder with the misalignment case. State the invariant — interior chunks must be shard-multiples, tail may be short — and verify it explicitly.

issues.description: Test `test_zarr_risky_shards_warns` uses `pytest.raises(PerformanceWarning)`, locking in the undecided semantic.
issues.detail: The test name says 'warns' but the assertion uses `pytest.raises`, encoding the raise-vs-warn confusion into the suite. Whichever way the design question resolves, the test must change shape. Decide the contract first, then rename and rewrite the test against it (pytest.warns vs pytest.raises with a proper exception class).

issues.description: Open design decision (config vs shard-shape precedence) is unresolved in code and comments.
issues.detail: The PR description asks what should win when global `array.chunk-size` competes with shard shape, and the diff silently chooses raise without recording the policy near the call site. Resolve it explicitly — which value wins and why — and leave a short comment at the raise/warn site so the next maintainer inherits the decision, not the question.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on NEEDS-WORK. The directional move — using shard shape as `previous_chunks` so `auto_chunks` produces shard-aligned chunks — is sound, but the safety net ships with three structural failures: an unreachable `break` after `raise` (proving the failure path never executed), `raise PerformanceWarning` conflating warning semantics with hard refusal, and a `safe_chunk_size` formula whose arithmetic doesn't match the per-axis divisibility check it's meant to remediate. The divisibility check itself inspects only `dw[0]` without stating its invariant, and the test locks the undecided raise-vs-warn semantic in via `pytest.raises`. Resolve the warn-vs-raise design question first; the dead code, byte math, and test shape all fall out of that decision.
